<!-- fathom:owned — generated by `fathom init --skills`; safe to delete this line to adopt the file as your own -->

## Running the gate

```sh
fathom verify --service <svc> --plan docs/plans/<plan>.md
```

- `--service` is required — the service ID fathom indexed this repo under
  (defaults to the repo directory's lowercased basename if you used
  `fathom init` with no `--service` override).
- `--plan` is repeatable — pass it more than once to gate several plans in
  one invocation.
- Talks to the daemon over HTTP by default (`--url`, default
  `http://localhost:7575` or `$FATHOM_HTTP`). Pass `--store <path>` (a
  `.sqlite`/`.db` file) to verify directly against a store,
  bypassing the daemon entirely — this is what CI should do (build its own
  store, never trust a live daemon).
- `--strict`: claimed-but-`Unknown` tasks (e.g. no-contract lines, or a
  symbol the gate can't yet resolve) become gate **failures** too. Always
  add this in CI.
- `--require-all`: the wave gate (ADR-018 §2) — additionally fails on any
  `[ ]` open or `[~]` in-progress task, so a wave only passes once every row
  is claimed-and-verified or explicitly `[-]` skipped.
- `--concern <name>`: scopes contradiction-checking to a concern.
- `--json`: machine-readable report instead of the human table.
- `--quiet-pass`: suppress output entirely when the gate passes (exit 0) —
  useful in a pre-push hook that only wants to be noisy on failure.

## Exit codes — the contract that makes this a gate worth keeping

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | Every claimed (`[x]`) task verified | Nothing — proceed |
| `1` | A claimed task failed verification | **This is real** — the claim is wrong, not the gate. Fix the code, or uncheck the box. Never re-run hoping it changes. |
| `2` | Operational error — daemon unreachable, service not indexed, or the index is genuinely empty | **Fail-open, not a verdict on the plan.** Ingest the service and retry; do not treat this as "the plan is bad." |

In a pre-push hook (fail-open on 2): allow the push through on exit 2 with a
warning, block only on exit 1. In CI, treat exit 2 as a **failure** too — CI
builds its own store, so "daemon down" should never be a valid CI state
there.

**The empty-index honesty rule.** If verify looks like it's failing *every*
task, check `list_services` (or `fathom inspect`) first — a genuinely empty
index for that service is an operational error (exit 2), never "all claims
false." An index with zero symbols cannot prove or disprove anything.

**`test_reaches` is not `runtime_pass`.** A passing verdict means a `Test*`
function **statically reaches** the claimed symbol via the call graph — it
is never proof the test passes or even runs. Runtime evidence is a separate,
not-yet-ingested tier.

## Computed progress: `fathom plans status` / `fathom plans next`

State here is always **derived from the index**, never asserted — that's the
whole point of the gate.

```sh
fathom plans status --service <svc>   # per-plan rollup
fathom plans next   --service <svc>   # the ordered work frontier
```

- `plans status` (defaults to every `docs/plans/*.md` if `--plan` is
  omitted) prints a per-plan table: `total`, `proven`, `claimed-unproven`,
  `open`, `deferred`, `other-skipped`. Every row lands in exactly one
  bucket.
- `plans next` lists, in the order authored in the plan file, every row that
  still needs attention: `open`/`in-progress` rows plus rows the engine
  can't currently prove (`claimed-failing`, `claimed-unknown`) — each with
  its `{symbol, package}` anchor. This is the work frontier for whoever
  picks up the plan next; a plan with "no open work" here is one CI will
  actually pass.
- Both accept `--store <path>` for direct mode or `--url` for a
  non-default daemon, and `--json` for machine output.

## Reading a failing task

The human-text report expands failing criteria for any claimed task that
gates:

```
✗ [T-3] Add the retry wrapper {id: T-3, symbol: withRetry, package: internal/http}
    symbol_present: "withRetry" not found in the index
```

Fix the underlying claim (rename the symbol annotation to match reality, add
the missing code, or move the box back to `[ ]`/`[-]` with a disposition) —
never edit the checkbox alone to make the report quieter.
